title: The laser never points at a person

rule.explorer: Never look at the red dot. Point it at the wall.
rule.builder: Never shine the laser at eyes - yours, anyone's, or a pet's. Always aim it at a wall, below head height.
rule.engineer: Laser modules like this are Class 2/3R. The blink reflex is NOT reliable protection. Never aim at people, pets, vehicles or aircraft, never view the beam through a magnifier, telescope or camera lens, and always aim at a matte surface below eye level.

title: Science fruit is not snack fruit

rule.explorer: This fruit is for science. We do not eat it. Wash hands!
rule.builder: Once metal goes into the fruit, the fruit is science equipment, not food. Throw it away afterwards and wash your hands.
rule.engineer: Galvanized nails are zinc-coated and the copper electrode corrodes into the flesh. Both leach into the fruit. Bin it after the experiment and wash your hands.

rule.explorer: Never let the two battery wires touch.
rule.builder: If you connect the battery's + wire straight to its - wire, the battery gets hot fast. Always send the electricity through something first.
rule.engineer: A short circuit across the battery draws current limited only by internal resistance. A 9V alkaline will get hot; a lithium cell can vent. There must always be a resistive load in the loop.

title: Parts get hot when they're wired wrong

rule.explorer: If something feels hot, tell a grown-up.
rule.builder: Touch a resistor after a few minutes. Warm is fine. Too hot to touch means something is wrong - unplug the battery and check your wiring.
rule.engineer: P = I x V. A quarter-watt resistor dissipating more than 0.25W will scorch. If a part is too hot to hold, disconnect and recheck your resistor value.

title: Nails and wire ends are sharp

rule.explorer: A grown-up pushes the nail in.
rule.builder: Push nails into fruit slowly, away from your other hand. Cut wire ends are sharp too.
rule.engineer: Push electrodes in with the fruit resting on the table, never held in your palm. Freshly cut jumper ends are sharp enough to break skin.

title: Small parts are not for mouths

rule.explorer: Parts stay on the table, never in your mouth.
rule.builder: LEDs, resistors and transistors are choking hazards for little kids. Keep them in the tray.
rule.engineer: Keep loose components in a closed tray when a toddler is in the room.
